rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=bilateral, bilateral_on_top=False, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=30, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-27 param_efficient breast -- DIAGNOSTIC: CG-DC WITHOUT LPD-combine (isolate the mismatch). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: CG-DC + LPD-combine gave 0.2362 (n_cg5) / 0.2427 (n_cg2, 5ep) -- far below filtered-DC+LPD 0.5047 AND below filtered-DC+bilateral 0.4345 (iter-11). iter-26 reached 5 epochs (not just starved), so the pattern = INTEGRATION MISMATCH: the CG least-squares solution doesn't compose with the LPD-combine, which learned to route the SINGLE filtered-gradient correction. (2) FAILURE MODE (to isolate): is CG-DC bad vs filtered-DC in general, or only bad WITH the LPD-combine? (3) ONE KNOB: lpd_on True->False on the CG-DC config (raw CG-DC prox-grad unroll + 3-scale bilateral gate, the iter-11 structure but with dc_mode=cg instead of filtered). n_cg=2, K=30, seed42, ~15 params. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if raw CG-DC + bilateral reaches ~0.4345 (filtered-DC+bilateral's level), the problem is specifically CG-DC-vs-LPD-combine (CG doesn't compose with the learned router) -> filtered-gradient is the right DC for the LPD-combine. If raw CG-DC + bilateral ALSO underperforms filtered-DC+bilateral, then CG-DC is just worse per-projector-call under the wall regardless of the combiner. Either way isolates the finding. (5) BUDGET: n_cg=2 x K=30 + bilateral, train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min comparable. (6) SERIAL; iter-28: CONCLUDE CG-DC, then continue menu (multi-scale bilateral POST-filter, learned per-step DC schedule, 2-step LPD)., dc_mode=cg, per_step_alpha=False, cg_n=2, cg_lam_init=0.01, lpd_on=False
